A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same work, Simple Guidance Mechanisms for Discrete Diffusion Models. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling and guided-generation experiments in Section 5, with hyperparameter studies and unconditional-generation results in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including perplexity measurements, controlled-generation evaluations, ablations, and generated samples.

M1.justification: D-CFG, D-CBG, the optional first-order approximation, the uniform-noise denoiser, and the continuous-time training objective are retained. Notation corrections and additional preprocessing documentation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Species10, QM9, CIFAR10, text8, Amazon Polarity, and LM1B, retaining the same language-modeling, controlled-generation, and unconditional-generation tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including AR, MDLM, FUDGE, PPLM, NOS, and the language-modeling baselines in Tables 2–3. Shortened names and revised citation formatting do not introduce different baselines.

E3.justification: The reported splits, model sizes, training budgets, sampling procedures, and metric definitions are retained. The added specification of QM9 padding direction documents an existing setting without establishing a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The continuous-time comparison in Figure 2 and Appendix D's guidance-strength, sampling-step, and first-order-approximation studies are retained. Renumbered tables and figures report the same analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed means and standard deviations for the genomic and molecular generation experiments. Rounding uncertainty values in the merged main table does not change the reporting practice; detailed appendix values remain.

E6.justification: v2 removes the random-sequence baseline's 3-mer and 6-mer JS scores, 0.13 and 0.22, from Table 4; these are absent from the appendix. It also removes v1 Figure 4's class-labelled CIFAR10 sample gallery and Table 1's observation of AR overfitting. Matched model scores remain unchanged; merged molecule tables introduce only rounding.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 corrects the meaning of the transition-matrix entry from an i-to-j transition to a j-to-i transition, aligning it with the stated matrix multiplication. The UDLM derivation and proofs in Appendices A–B are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about discrete guidance, the continuous-time uniform-noise objective, small-vocabulary performance, and improved controllable generation.

C2.justification: The explanations linking repeated token editing to controllability and fast sampling, vocabulary size to modeling difficulty, and approximation choices to MDLM instability are retained. References to correcting errors and long-sequence costs restate explanations already present in v1.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a direct QM9 tokenizer link and specifies right-sided padding for the existing 32-token inputs. These improve implementation documentation; other architecture, training, hardware, and access information is retained.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces Lou et al. (2023) with Shi et al. (2024) when attributing the inability to repeatedly edit generated tokens. This is a limited correction to prior-work attribution; the bibliography and broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 tightens several main-text paragraphs and captions, standardizes terminology and notation, adds a table of contents, and updates publication status and author credits. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The main empirical presentation is substantially reorganized: v1 Tables 5–6 become one side-by-side molecule table, several tables are resized and wrapped into prose, Table 4 drops its JS columns, and the fast-sampling table drops its F1 column. The class-labelled CIFAR10 gallery is removed, while the separate appendix guidance-strength gallery remains.

improvement.justification: The corrected transition definition, explicit tokenizer and padding information, and added contents improve precision, reproducibility, and navigation. Condensation loses two reference scores, a sample gallery, and some explanatory detail, but preserves the principal numerical evidence and appendix settings. These changes provide a modest overall benefit without substantially strengthening the scientific contribution.
